You build something valuable — an ebook, a course, a Notion template, a font family, a preset pack, a beat — and someone pays you for access to it. The file transfers. The transaction completes. But for millions of creators, the payment layer is where [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/everything-you-need-know-about-sovereign-commerce-infrastructure-2|Everything You]]-you-need-know-about-google-apps-script-3|everything]] breaks down. Stripe is unavailable. PayPal flags the account. Gumroad holds the payout. The workarounds stop working. What actually works is a sovereign commerce stack: a static storefront on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, automatic payment verification through NOWPayments, and delivery triggered by a webhook the moment the transaction confirms on-chain. No platform intermediary. No payout schedule. No geography filter. The customer owns the storefront code, the order history, the customer list, and the product files. COREMERCH has no access after deployment.

content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Automated ebook

The real architecture behind automated ebook delivery after crypto payment is a complex system that ensures secure and efficient transactions. It involves the use of cryptocurrencies, such as Bitcoin or Ethereum, to facilitate payments, and a network of servers and databases to manage the delivery of digital products. This system is crucial for digital creators who want to maintain control over their sales and distribution processes.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The architecture works by using a combination of cloud-based services, such as GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, to host the digital products, and a backend logic system, such as Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, to manage the payment and delivery processes. The system also utilizes a database, such as Supabase or Google Sheets, to store order information and track deliveries.
Who This Is Built For and Why

The product types that work with automated crypto delivery are any digital files that can be stored and delivered via download link: ebooks in PDF or EPUB format, courses packaged as ZIP archives, Notion templates exported as files or share links, font families as ZIP archives of OTF and TTF files, Lightroom or Capture One preset packs, beat files as WAV or MP3 archives, plugin installers, stock photo packs, software license keys, and any other file-based product. The delivery system in Stack 01 uses Google Drive shared links. Stack 02 uses Cloudflare R2 presigned URLs with configurable expiry times — typically 24 to 72 hours — which prevents download links from being shared indefinitely after a single purchase.
Deploy a sovereign commerce infrastructure today.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The order management layer gives you complete visibility into every transaction your store processes. In Stack 01, every order is logged to a Google Sheet with the buyer's email, product purchased, payment amount in crypto and USD equivalent, transaction hash for on-chain verification, and delivery status. In Stack 02, orders are stored in a Supabase PostgreSQL database with the same fields plus additional metadata. Both can be exported as CSV at any time. The transaction hash provides cryptographic proof of every payment that does not depend on any platform's records — you can verify any transaction independently on a public blockchain explorer.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

To deploy this system today, digital creators can start by setting up a cloud-based hosting service, such as GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, and a backend logic system, such as Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script. They can then integrate a payment gateway, such as NOWPayments, to facilitate crypto payments, and a database, such as Supabase or Google Sheets, to store order information and track deliveries.
What is the best crypto payment gateway?

The fastest path to your first sovereign digital product sale is a three-step process. First, create a NOWPayments account — configure your wallet addresses for USDT on Tron and Bitcoin as starting points, generate your API key, and set the webhook endpoint URL. Second, choose your stack: Stack 01 uses GitHub Pages plus Google Apps Script and takes most creators four to six hours following the Sovereign Blueprint at $47; Stack 02 uses Cloudflare Pages plus Workers plus Supabase and is deployed by COREMERCH in 48 hours with the Edge Commerce Stack at $197. Third, upload your product files, set your prices in USD, and run a complete mainnet test transaction before promoting.
Take control of your sales and distribution processes.
Related: How Creators Like You Are Building Sovereign Stores

Digital creators selling ebooks, courses, templates, fonts, presets, and beats often reach this infrastructure question after hitting payout restrictions or platform policy problems on Gumroad, Payhip, or Lemon Squeezy. The difference with a sovereign stack is structural: there is no platform relationship to manage, no content policy to comply with, and no payout schedule to wait on. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 deploys the complete infrastructure in 48 hours under your own accounts. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the build process for creators who prefer to self-deploy. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy a sovereign commerce infrastructure, follow these steps: set up a cloud-based hosting service, integrate a backend logic system, set up a payment gateway, integrate a database, and test the system to ensure it is working correctly. By following these steps, digital creators can maintain control over their sales and distribution processes and ensure reliable and efficient delivery of their digital products.
